title: Yesterday — and the نے that flips the sentence
goal: Tell what you did yesterday, and master the marker نے, which makes a past-tense verb agree with the object, not the subject. This is the hardest and most important unit in the whole module.
bekal: forming the past of any verb
making past verbs agree with the object correctly

dialogs.title: مکالمہ — کل کیا ہوا؟
dialogs.intro: The next morning on campus. Ayesha wants to know how Budi's visit to Hasan's house went.

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: میں نے حسن کے گھر میں کھانا کھایا۔
lines.baca: maiñ ne Hasan ke ghar meñ khānā khāyā.
lines.literal: I (ne) Hasan of house in food eaten(m).

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: ان کی امی نے بریانی بنائی۔ بہت مزیدار تھی۔
lines.baca: un kī ammī ne biryānī banāī. bahut mazedār thī.
lines.id: His mom made biryani. It was delicious.
lines.literal: his(f) mother (ne) biryani made(f). very tasty was(f).

lines.speaker: عائشہ:
lines.text: واہ! آپ نے چائے بھی پی؟
lines.baca: vāh! āp ne chāe bhī pī?
lines.id: Wow! Did you have tea too?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: جی، دو کپ۔ پھر ہم نے باتیں کیں۔
lines.baca: jī, do kap. phir ham ne bāteñ kīñ.
lines.id: Yes, two cups. Then we chatted.
lines.literal: yes, two cups. then we (ne) talks done(f-pl).

lines.speaker: عائشہ:
lines.id: What time did you get home?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: میں گیارہ بجے آیا۔ بارش ہو رہی تھی۔
lines.baca: maiñ gyārah baje āyā. bārish ho rahī thī.
lines.id: I got home at eleven. It was raining then.
lines.literal: I eleven o'clock came(m). rain happen staying was(f).

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: نہیں، میں بھول گیا! میں بھیگ گیا۔
lines.baca: nahīñ, maiñ bhūl gayā! maiñ bhīg gayā.
lines.id: No, I forgot! I got soaked.
lines.literal: no, I forget went(m)! I soak went(m).

lines.speaker: عائشہ:
lines.id: Oh no! Are you all right today?

lines.speaker: بودی:
lines.text: جی، بالکل ٹھیک ہوں۔ کھانا اس کے قابل تھا!
lines.baca: jī, bilkul ṭhīk hūñ. khānā us ke qābil thā!
lines.id: Yes, totally fine. The food was worth it!
lines.literal: yes, completely fine am. food its worth was(m)!

notes: **This is the hardest pattern in Urdu, and it's worth reading twice.** If the verb is **transitive** — it has an object — and the sentence is in the **past**, then the subject takes the marker **نے**, and the verb **agrees with the object**, not the subject. میں نے بریانی کھائی: the verb کھائی is feminine because **بریانی** is feminine, even though the person eating is male.

**Compare two sentences next to each other in the dialog.** The sentence میں گیارہ بجے آیا has no نے, because آنا has no object — so the verb agrees with **the speaker**, giving آیا for a man. The sentence میں نے چائے پی uses نے, and the verb agrees with **چائے**, which is feminine, giving پی. Two sentences, two different rules, and only one thing decides: is there an object?

**Which verbs take نے?** The ones with an object: کھانا (eat), پینا (drink), دیکھنا (see), پڑھنا (read), لکھنا (write), کرنا (do), خریدنا (buy), لینا (take), دینا (give), بنانا (make), سننا (hear), کہنا (say). The ones without: جانا، آنا، اٹھنا، سونا، بیٹھنا، ہنسنا، رونا، پہنچنا.

**⚠️ Four verbs that have an object but do NOT take نے.** لانا (bring), بھولنا (forget), ملنا (meet, get), بولنا (speak). These are exceptions to memorize, and there's no reason behind them — just the way the language works. میں بھول گیا, not میں نے بھولا.

**The word تھا is the past of "is".** تھا (m sg), تھی (f sg), تھے (m pl), تھیں (f pl). بریانی مزیدار تھی = "the biryani was delicious". It also attaches to the end of the "-ing" form to describe something that was going on in the past: بارش ہو رہی تھی ("it was raining").

**Compound verbs with جانا mark something completed.** میں بھول گیا isn't just "I forgot" but "I went and forgot, and it's done". میں بھیگ گیا = "I got soaked". This pattern is the heart of conversational Urdu and is covered fully at A2 — for now, just recognize that گیا after another verb doesn't mean "went".

grammars.title: Forming the past
body: Take the root of the verb, then attach one of four endings. There's no "is" to add — the verb stands on its own.

head: Ending
Used when the agreeing word is
Example
Meaning

after: Six irregular forms, and that's all of them: the past of کرنا is کیا · the past of جانا is گیا · the past of لینا is لیا · the past of دینا is دیا · the past of پینا is پیا · and the past of ہونا is ہوا. Every other Urdu verb follows the table above with no surprises — a very short list compared with English.
Roots ending in a vowel insert ی or ئ so they can be read — from کھانا come کھایا، کھائی، کھائے. That's a spelling matter, not grammar.

grammars.title: Two paths, and how to choose in three seconds
body: Every time you build a past sentence, ask one question: **does this verb have an object?** The answer decides the whole shape of the sentence.

head: No object
With an object
rows: میں نے چائے پی۔ — I drank tea
میں نے چائے پی۔ — I drank tea

after: ⚠️ Look at rows three and four: on the **with-object** path, the male and female sentences are **exactly the same**. This is where Urdu stops caring about the speaker's gender — and you can use it as a memory hook: once نے appears, forget yourself and look at the object.

⚠️ If the object takes the marker کو — for example, a specific person — the verb loses its anchor and falls back to the **neutral ـا** form: میں نے علی کو دیکھا and میں نے عائشہ کو دیکھا. Both use دیکھا.

blocks.text: With an object — notice the form no longer depends on the speaker

blocks.title: Pronoun forms before نے
items: Pronouns change shape once نے attaches: میں becomes میں نے · تم becomes تم نے · آپ becomes آپ نے · یہ and وہ become اس نے · ہم becomes ہم نے · and plural وہ becomes انہوں نے.

The form انہوں نے often surprises learners because it looks nothing like وہ. It's also used for **one respected person**: ان کی امی نے بریانی بنائی — "his mom made biryani", with the respectful plural.

The fastest way to master this unit isn't memorizing tables but **writing five sentences about your own yesterday**, then checking each one: is there an object or not? Is the object masculine or feminine? After twenty sentences, your hand just knows.

exercises.prompt: Write نے where needed, or a dash where it isn't.

items: Yesterday I ate at a friend's house.
I drank two cups of tea.
I forgot to bring an umbrella.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: نے — no نے — نے — no نے — نے
پی — کھایا — پڑھیں — گیا، آیا — دیکھی
کل میں نے دوست کے گھر میں کھانا کھایا۔ — میں نے دو کپ چائے پی۔ — اس نے خط لکھا۔ — میں گیارہ بجے واپس آیا۔ — میں چھتری لانا بھول گیا۔
میں نے کھانا کھایا۔ — آپ نے چائے پی؟ — میں گیارہ بجے آیا۔ — امی نے بریانی بنائی۔ — ہم نے فلم دیکھی۔
wave: This unit won't sink in on one reading, and that's normal. Write five sentences about your yesterday every day for a week, then check each نے one by one.
